The test image shows a corn plant viewed from below. Key observations:
- The tassel/growing point area shows abnormal, twisted, dried brown structures instead of a normal tassel
- The upper portion has proliferating leaf-like and dried material emerging from the whorl area
- Leaves appear otherwise green and healthy

Top candidates: **Crazy_top** (proliferating leafy tassel), **Head_smut** (smutted tassel mass), **Downy_mildew** (systemic infection). Let me check references.

The Crazy_top reference (top-right panel) is nearly identical to the test image — same view angle, same proliferating leafy/dried structures at the growing point against blue sky. Head_smut shows black spore masses (doesn't match). Downy_mildew shows pale striped leaves (doesn't match).

Let me check a couple more to confirm:

All other candidates are clearly ruled out:
- **Anthracnose_leaf_spot**: discrete necrotic spots on leaves — no match
- **Common_smut**: large galls on ear/tassel — no match
- **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma**: purple/red striping on mature senescing plants — no match
- **Stewarts_wilt / Gray_leaf_spot / NCLB**: all show leaf lesion patterns — no match
- **Goss_wilt, MDMV, Maize_streak**: leaf mosaic/streak/wilt patterns — no match

The test image shows exactly what Crazy_top causes: the tassel replaced by a proliferating mass of twisted, leafy, chaotic structures with dried/brown material — the "crazy" growth phenotype — photographed from below against a blue sky. The top-right panel of the Crazy_top reference collage is a near-identical match to the test image.
